# Cache Controller Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The cache controller is the front-end for data cache accesses. It accepts one memory request at a time, determines whether the access is cacheable, performs a cache tag lookup, handles cache hits and misses, and coordinates with the miss/refill path for loads that miss and for uncached accesses.

The cache is set-associative. A cache line contains two 64-bit words, so the addressed word is selected by the word-offset bits of the address. The number of ways, address bit widths, and the cacheable region boundary are compile-time parameters.

## 2. Reset and Idle Behavior

After reset, the controller shall be idle. In the idle state:

- The busied indication shall be deasserted.
- No read data shall be returned.
- No miss/refill request shall be pending.
- No cache-array write shall be issued.

The controller shall remain idle until a new memory request is presented and no flush condition is active.

## 3. Request Acceptance

A memory request includes:

- The address, from which the cache index, tag, and word offset are derived.
- A read/write indication.
- Byte enables identifying which bytes in the 64-bit data word are valid.
- The access size.
- The write data for stores.

For a cacheable load, the controller may indicate acceptance as soon as the cache lookup is started. For a cacheable store, the controller shall indicate completion only when the store has been safely accepted by either the cache array or the miss/refill path.

A kill indication shall take priority over normal operation. When asserted, the controller shall abandon the current operation and return to idle so that a new request can be accepted.

## 4. Cacheability

The controller shall treat an access as uncacheable in either of the following situations:

- The cache bypass mode is active.
- The address falls below the configured cacheable region boundary.

Uncacheable accesses shall not update or allocate cache lines. They shall be handled through the miss/refill path instead.

## 5. Cache Lookup

For a cacheable access, the controller shall perform a lookup in the cache array using the address index. The lookup shall examine all ways and determine whether any way contains the requested tag.

- If a way matches, the access is a cache hit.
- If no way matches, the access is a cache miss.

The controller shall not modify cache contents as a result of a lookup alone.

## 6. Read Behavior

### 6.1 Read Hit

When a cacheable read hits:

- The controller shall return the addressed 64-bit word from the matching cache line.
- The returned word shall be indicated as valid.
- The read is then complete.
- A read hit shall not alter the cached data or metadata.

### 6.2 Read Miss

When a cacheable read misses:

- The controller shall issue a miss/refill request for the missing cache line.
- The request shall include the line address, byte enables, access size, and read/write indication.
- The controller shall not issue a duplicate miss request if the same line is already being served by an outstanding miss.
- When the requested word of the refill is delivered, the controller shall return that word and indicate that it is valid.
- The read is complete when that requested word is returned.

## 7. Write Behavior

### 7.1 Write Hit

When a cacheable write hits:

- The controller shall merge the write data into the matching cache line at the addressed word.
- Only bytes selected by the byte enables shall be updated.
- The matching line shall be marked valid and dirty.
- The write shall be indicated as complete only after the cache array accepts the update.
- Before the update is finalized, the controller shall verify that no outstanding miss aliases the same cache index. If such an alias exists, the store shall be deferred until the miss completes.

### 7.2 Write Miss

When a cacheable write misses:

- The controller shall issue a miss/refill request carrying the write data, byte enables, access size, and write indication.
- Once the miss/refill path accepts the write request, the controller shall indicate store completion and return to idle.
- The controller shall not wait for a cache-line refill before completing the store.

## 8. Uncached and Bypass Accesses

When an access is uncacheable:

- The controller shall route it to the miss/refill path as an uncached request.
- The cache array shall not be written or updated.
- For an uncached read, the controller shall wait until the uncached read data is returned, then present that data as the valid read result.
- For an uncached write, the controller shall report completion when the uncached write transaction completes.

## 9. Aliasing with Outstanding Misses

The controller shall make the current access address available for comparison with outstanding misses and shall obey the comparison result.

- If the requested address matches an outstanding miss, the controller shall not issue a new miss request.
- Instead, it shall wait until no matching miss remains.
- After the match clears, the controller shall re-access the cache array, because the line may now have been filled.

Store completion requires additional protection. A store hit shall be held off if any outstanding miss targets the same cache index, regardless of whether the tag matches. This prevents a write from updating a cache line that is about to be replaced by a refill.

## 10. Flush Behavior

A flush indication shall prevent the start of any new memory request. A request that is already in progress may continue until it completes or is killed.

If flush is asserted while the controller is idle, requests shall not leave the idle condition.

## 11. Back-to-Back Requests

The controller may accept a new request while completing the current read response, provided the cache array or refill path can accept the new access. If no resource is available, the controller shall return to idle and accept the new request later.

## 12. Busy Indication

The controller shall assert the busy indication whenever it is not idle. The busy indication shall be deasserted when the controller returns to the idle state.

## 13. Cache Line Size Assumption

The controller assumes each cache line is exactly 128 bits wide, organized as two 64-bit words. The address selects one of the two words, and byte enables qualify bytes within that word. This assumption must hold for the configured cache geometry.

# Cache Miss Handler — Behavioral Design Specification

## 1. Purpose and Scope
This module services cache-miss and bypass requests from a configurable number of request ports. It manages cache-line refills, dirty-line writebacks, full-cache flushes, and uncached bypass traffic. It exposes two logical external-memory interfaces: one for full cache-line refill and writeback traffic, and one for uncached single-beat bypass traffic. It also reads and writes the local cache data and status array.

## 2. Reset and Initialization
After reset, the module shall initialize the cache status array. It shall mark every cache line as invalid and clean before accepting any miss, bypass, or flush operation. Until initialization completes, the module shall remain unresponsive to functional requests.

## 3. Request Port Model
Each request port may present a request characterized by:
- a valid indication,
- a bypass versus cached classification,
- an address,
- a read/write direction,
- write data and byte-enable information,
- transfer size.

A bypass request shall be treated as an uncached access to external memory. A non-bypass request shall be treated as a cache miss that requires the addressed cache line to be refilled.

## 4. Flush Operation
When a flush request is accepted, flush processing shall take precedence over new cache-miss requests. The module shall scan the entire cache index range. At each index it shall read all ways of the status/data array. For every way that is valid and dirty, the module shall:
1. select that way as a victim,
2. write the victim’s full data and tag back to external memory via the cache-line interface,
3. clear the dirty and valid status bits for that way.

After processing every index, the module shall assert the flush-complete indication and return to the idle state.

## 5. Cache-Miss Handling
When a non-bypass request is accepted, the module shall begin servicing the miss and shall not accept another non-bypass miss until the current one completes.

The module shall read the addressed cache set. It shall select a target way as follows:
- If any way in the set is invalid, it shall select one invalid way.
- If all ways are valid, it shall select a victim way using a pseudo-random replacement policy.

If the selected way is dirty, the module shall first write back the full cache line to external memory, invalidate the way, and only then request the refill. If the selected way is not dirty, the module shall invalidate the way and request the refill directly.

The module shall request a full cache-line read from the refill/writeback memory interface using the cache-line-aligned address of the missed access.

When the refill data returns, the module shall write the new cache line into the selected way, set the line valid, and initially clean. If the original request was a write, the module shall merge the write data according to the byte enables into the corresponding bytes of the new line and mark the line dirty.

After the refill is completed and the cache array is updated, the module shall clear the outstanding miss and become ready to accept another miss.

## 6. Critical-Word Delivery
During a cache-line refill, the module shall identify the 64-bit word that corresponds to the original request address within the line. It shall output that word on the critical-word data output and assert the critical-word-valid indication when that word becomes available.

## 7. Bypass Transactions
For requests classified as bypass, the module shall perform an uncached single-beat read or write transaction on the bypass memory interface using the request’s address, data, byte enables, direction, and size. When multiple bypass requests are pending, the module shall select one request and assert the bypass grant indication for that port; other pending ports shall remain un-granted until the current transaction completes.

For a bypass read, when the response returns, the module shall assert the bypass response-valid indication for the requesting port and drive the read data onto the bypass read-data output. For a bypass write, the module shall signal completion via the bypass response-valid indication.

## 8. Active-Serving Indication
The module shall continuously indicate which request port, if any, is currently being serviced for a cache miss. This indication shall be asserted for the entire duration of the miss service and de-asserted when the miss is complete.

## 9. Outstanding-Miss Address Matching
The module shall provide two match indications for each request port relative to the currently outstanding cache miss:
- **Address match**: asserted when the port’s address matches the outstanding miss address excluding the byte offset.
- **Index match**: asserted when the port’s address matches the outstanding miss cache index.

Both indications shall be de-asserted when no miss is outstanding.

## 10. Performance Indication
The module shall assert a miss-indication output while a cache miss is being processed. This output is intended for performance monitoring and shall not be asserted during bypass or flush operations.

## 11. Cache Array Interface
When reading a cache set, the module shall request all ways at the target set index. For writes resulting from a refill, an eviction status update, or initialization, the module shall write only the selected way(s) and update the relevant tag, valid, and dirty fields.

## 12. Coexistence and Priority
- Initialization has the highest priority after reset and must complete before functional operation begins.
- A flush request, once accepted, has priority over new cache-miss requests.
- Bypass transactions proceed independently of the cache-miss/refill state machine, subject only to arbitration among request ports.

# Behavioral Specification: Non-Blocking Level-1 Data Cache

## 1. Overview

This module implements a private, non-blocking Level-1 data cache. It provides cached memory service for multiple request streams, handles cache misses by fetching lines from memory, writes back dirty lines on eviction, supports atomic memory operations, and can bypass caching when disabled.

The cache shall:

- service loads, stores, and atomic memory operations;
- detect cache hits and misses;
- fetch missing cache lines on a miss;
- write back dirty lines on eviction and flush;
- support multiple outstanding misses without blocking all requestors;
- provide an uncached access path when caching is disabled;
- report flush completion and miss status to the external system.

## 2. Reset and Initial State

After reset:

- no cache line shall be considered valid;
- no dirty line shall be pending writeback;
- no request shall be granted;
- no load or AMO response shall be reported;
- no AMO result shall be valid;
- the cache shall behave as if it contains no usable data.

## 3. Request Port Behavior

The module shall provide three independent request ports. Each port may present a memory operation containing:

- an address, supplied as a cache index and tag;
- a read/write indication;
- write data and byte enables;
- an access size;
- an optional atomic-operation type;
- optional cancellation and tag-validity qualifiers.

For each port:

- A request is accepted only when the module asserts a grant.
- A request that is not granted must be held by the requestor until it is granted or canceled.
- A request canceled before grant shall have no effect on cache state and shall not produce a response.
- Once granted, the operation shall be performed and, where required, a response shall be generated.
- Load operations shall return 64 bits of requested data together with a response-valid indication.
- Store operations are complete when granted and do not require a data response.
- The ports shall be independent: a miss or long-latency operation on one port shall not prevent the other ports from making forward progress.

## 4. Cache Hit Behavior

For an accepted request with a valid tag:

- The module shall look up the addressed cache set.
- A hit occurs when the presented tag matches a valid line in that set.

On a load hit:

- The requested data shall be returned to the requestor.
- The cache line shall not be modified.

On a store hit:

- The store data shall be written into the addressed bytes.
- Bytes not selected by the byte enables shall be preserved.
- The affected cache line shall be marked dirty so that it will later be written back to memory.

On an atomic-operation hit:

- The addressed memory word shall be read.
- The specified atomic operation shall be performed.
- The result shall be written back to the cache line.
- The line shall be marked dirty.
- The value read before the operation shall be returned as the AMO result.

Requests whose tag-validity qualifier is not asserted shall not be allowed to hit or update cache state.

## 5. Cache Miss and Refill Behavior

If no valid cache line matches the presented tag, the operation is a miss.

On a miss:

- The module shall indicate that a miss has occurred.
- The request shall remain accepted and tracked; the requestor shall not need to retry the request.
- A line refill shall be initiated from the refill memory interface.

For a load miss:

- The load result may be delivered as soon as the requested word has been fetched.
- It shall not be necessary to wait for the entire cache line to be filled before returning the load data.

For a store miss:

- The cache line shall be fetched before the store is applied.
- After the line is available, the store bytes shall be written into the line and the line shall be marked dirty.

For an atomic-operation miss:

- The cache line shall be fetched before the atomic operation is performed.
- After the line is available, the read-modify-write operation shall be performed and the result returned.

Miss handling shall be non-blocking:

- Multiple misses may be outstanding simultaneously.
- A miss on one request port shall not block hit processing on other ports.
- If multiple outstanding misses target the same cache line, the module shall avoid fetching the same line more than once and shall satisfy all waiting requests when the line becomes available.

When a miss requires allocating a new line in a set that is already full:

- A line in that set shall be selected for replacement.
- If the selected line is dirty, it shall be written back to memory.
- The new line shall not overwrite data that has not yet been safely written back.

## 6. Bypass Mode

When caching is disabled, the cache shall operate in bypass mode.

In bypass mode:

- All requests shall be treated as uncached.
- No cache line shall be allocated, updated, or invalidated because of a normal load or store.
- Loads shall be forwarded to the bypass memory interface, and the data returned from memory shall be delivered to the requestor.
- Stores shall be forwarded to memory and shall not be cached.
- Atomic operations shall be performed on memory without allocating a cache line.
- Cache contents shall not be used to satisfy any request in bypass mode.

## 7. Cache Flush

The module shall support a flush operation that makes the cache empty and ensures that all dirty data is written back.

When a flush is requested:

- The module shall complete or drain operations that are required for a consistent final state.
- Dirty cache lines shall be written back to memory.
- All cache lines shall be invalidated.
- The flush shall not be acknowledged until all necessary writebacks have completed.

When the flush is complete:

- The module shall assert a flush-acknowledge indication.
- The acknowledge shall be a single-cycle pulse.
- If no dirty lines and no outstanding operations exist, the flush shall be acknowledged promptly.

## 8. Atomic Memory Operation Behavior

The module shall support the atomic operations defined by the request encoding.

Each atomic memory operation shall:

- read the addressed memory word;
- compute the operation result;
- write the result back to the same address;
- return the old value read from memory as the AMO result.

Atomic operations must be atomic with respect to other memory operations on the memory interface.

The module shall also support commit and cancel control for AMOs:

- An AMO may be held pending until the external system either commits or cancels it.
- If the AMO is canceled, it shall have no memory side effect and no AMO result shall be reported.
- If the AMO is committed, it shall be performed exactly once and its result shall be reported on the AMO result output.
- The reported AMO result shall remain stable until the next AMO result is reported.

## 9. Memory Interface Behavior

The module shall use refill and bypass memory interfaces to perform external memory traffic.

The refill interface shall be used for:

- fetching missing cache lines;
- writing back dirty evicted lines;
- performing cache-line-sized memory transactions.

The bypass interface shall be used for:

- uncached accesses when caching is disabled;
- loads, stores, and atomics that must go directly to memory.

The module shall generate memory transactions that respect the configured cache line size, access size, and memory address alignment.

A load or AMO response shall not be reported to a requestor until the required data has been received from the memory interface.

## 10. Ordering and Forward Progress

The module shall preserve the memory ordering required by the processor for operations issued on the same request port.

The module shall not deadlock under normal operation:

- accepted requests shall eventually complete or be canceled;
- miss handling shall eventually make progress;
- flush shall eventually complete;
- all required responses shall be generated once their data is available.
